title: Learning Generalizable Program and Architecture Representations for Performance Modeling
problem: Existing performance modeling approaches suffer from high computational costs in discrete-event simulators, limited flexibility in hardware emulators, or restricted accuracy and generality in analytical and data-driven models.
motivation: Performance modeling is essential for characterizing system behavior, optimizing designs, conducting design space exploration, and making resource allocation decisions.
method: PerfVec uses deep learning to learn decoupled, orthogonal representations of programs and microarchitectures. A learned program representation generalizes across microarchitectures for performance prediction, and a microarchitecture representation applies across programs. The framework produces a foundation model capturing instruction-level performance semantics reusable without retraining.
key_novelty: Learning independent, orthogonal program and microarchitecture representations that enable bidirectional cross-generalization for performance prediction.
contributions: PerfVec framework for learning decoupled program and architecture representations
Foundation model encoding instruction-level performance characteristics
Cross-generalization capability enabling performance prediction across unseen architectures and programs
Demonstrated superiority in generality and efficiency over simulators, emulators, and analytical/data-driven models

metrics.other: efficiency gains claimed but not specified

primary_theme: Generalizable performance prediction via learned program and architecture representations
